pathway.title: Synchrony Financial — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Synchrony Financial funds its balance sheet mainly with deposits, which were USD 82,951 million at 2026-09-30 and 83% of funding sources, while borrowings were USD 17,025 million. Because debt due within one year of that date was USD 4,500 million against liquid assets of USD 19.5 billion, near-term maturities are covered several times by liquidity even before counting the USD 2,100 million of undrawn committed securitization capacity. This lowers refinancing and liquidity risk for creditors, and the main condition is continued access to deposits and the Federal Reserve discount window, whose availability was USD 13.0 billion.

The business depends on a short list of partners. The five largest programs produced 54% of interest and fees and 52% of loan receivables at year-end 2025, and three of them each exceeded a tenth of interest and fees; contract expiry dates run from 2030 to 2035, and some agreements let the partner buy the accounts on termination. A loss or repricing of one program would reduce revenue and the receivables book that backs the securitized notes and supports the bank, so concentration, not leverage, is the first risk a committee should monitor.

Earnings remain strong but are lower than a year earlier. Net earnings were USD 892 million in Q3 2026 against USD 1,077 million in the prior-year quarter, and USD 2,582 million for the nine months, while the net charge-off rate fell to 4.79% in Q3 2026 from 5.43% in Q2 2026. Retailer share arrangements of USD 3,193 million in the nine months move with program performance, so part of the benefit of better credit goes to partners and part of the pressure is absorbed by them. For debt service the only available proxy is 2.12x (pre-tax earnings plus interest expense, over interest expense, for the last twelve months), but that proxy includes deposit interest, is not an EBITDA measure, and the filings give no EBITDA.

Capital allocation is the main trend to monitor. Distributions in the nine months of 2026 were USD 3,262 million against net earnings of USD 2,582 million, which is 1.26x, while the common equity Tier 1 ratio on the recast basis moved from 13.5% at year-end 2025 to 12.9%, and borrowings to equity rose from 0.91x to 1.03x. New unsecured notes of USD 1,850 million and Series C preferred stock were issued in the same period. For creditors this means the equity buffer is being run down by choice and the company stays above stated regulatory minimums, so the pace of buybacks against capital targets is the variable to watch.

Structure matters for who holds which claim. Deposits are bank liabilities; securitized borrowings of USD 8,915 million are secured on restricted loans of USD 21,898 million, a ratio of 2.46x; the holding company owes about USD 7,511 million of senior and subordinated notes and relies on bank dividends and regulatory permission. Unsecured notes are 47.6% of borrowings, up from 44.6% at year-end 2025. The documented covenants restrict liens on and loss of control of the bank, and no leverage or restricted-payments test is visible, so legal capacity to distribute is not fully known.

cells.text: A consumer financial services company offering private label, dual, co-brand and general purpose credit cards, short- and long-term installment loans and consumer banking products
Revenue is interest, fees and merchant discounts on a receivables book, so earnings track balances, yield and credit losses

At 2026-09-30 credit cards were 92.4 percent of loan receivables, commercial credit products 2.6 percent and installment loans 4.9 percent; promotional financing (deferred interest 17.6 percent and other promotional 17.8 percent) sat alongside 64.6 percent on standard terms only
Promotional balances earn lower or no interest during the promotion and are compensated in part by merchant discounts from partners
Five platforms. Shares of total interest and fees on loans in FY2025: Home & Auto 26 percent, Digital 30 percent, Diversified & Value 22 percent, Health & Wellness 17 percent, Lifestyle 5 percent
Platforms differ in exposure: dental accounts were 49 percent of Health & Wellness interest and fees, and Health & Wellness has no single partner above 0.7 percent excluding Walgreens

The five largest programs (Amazon, Lowe's, PayPal, Sam's Club, TJX) were 54 percent of total interest and fees on loans and 52 percent of loan receivables at 2025-12-31; Lowe's, PayPal (including Venmo) and Sam's Club each exceeded 10 percent of interest and fees
Concentration makes revenue and portfolio ownership dependent on renewal and on partner health

Program agreements run about three to ten years with automatic renewal in many cases; large partner expiry dates range from 2030 through 2035; they can be terminated early for breach, adverse financial condition or change in law; some give the partner the right to buy the accounts at fair market value or a stated price
Partner purchase options and termination rights are a runoff and portfolio-loss mechanic, not a debt event

Most large retail and digital programs have retailer share arrangements paying the partner when economic performance exceeds a contractual threshold; FY2025 amount (4,005) and nine months 2026 amount (3,193)
Better credit performance raises the payment to partners, so part of the benefit of lower losses is shared; worse performance lowers it
Deposits were 83 percent of total funding sources at 2026-09-30, with direct deposits of 76.2 billion and brokered deposits of 6.8 billion; the rest is securitized and unsecured debt
Deposit funding lowers refinancing risk but binds the bank to regulatory liquidity and capital rules
Other expense nine months 2026 of 4,018, led by employee costs of 1,538 and information processing of 770; loyalty programmes are a deduction in other income (1,236)
Technology and operating loss costs rose against the prior-year period, with an efficiency ratio of 35.8 percent for the nine months against 33.4 percent a year earlier
Capital expenditure is not printed as a separate cash-flow line; the gross carrying amount of internal-use capitalized software was 3.4 billion at 2026-09-30

Allowance coverage and delinquency are generally higher at interim period ends, and loan balances and purchase volume have seasonal patterns
Quarterly comparisons must be seasonal; year-end figures are the cleaner comparison

A savings and loan holding company and financial holding company regulated by the Federal Reserve Board, the Bank by the OCC, and the CFPB for consumer finance; subject to constraints from having 100 billion or more in total assets
Capital, dividend and liquidity decisions at the parent depend on regulatory permission and on dividends from the Bank
The CEO describes the quarter as "another strong performance in the third quarter" and spend as reaching "a record third quarter level"

runs.text: Strengths. Deposit funding is the largest strength: it is diversified between direct deposits of USD 76.2 billion and brokered deposits of USD 6.8 billion, and it lowers rollover risk relative to market funding. Liquidity is large and not dependent on committed bank lines: liquid assets were USD 19.5 billion and discount window capacity USD 13.0 billion. Credit quality was supportive in Q3 2026, with the net charge-off rate lower than in Q2 2026, delinquencies of 4.34% at 30 days and 2.06% at 90 days, and an allowance of 10.01% of receivables. Contract tenure is long, with expiry dates for the largest partners from 2030, and regulatory capital is stated as above minimums with the Bank well capitalized. Nothing documented shows sponsor extraction or creditor-adverse behaviour.

Weaknesses. Concentration in five partner programs is the largest business weakness, and the partner purchase rights and termination terms are not in the sources. Earnings were below the prior-year quarter and a reserve build raised the provision. Distributions above earnings, a lower recast capital ratio and a rising unsecured share of borrowings reduce the margin beneath creditors. The structure places holding-company creditors behind deposits and trust investors for access to the bank's assets, and no parent-only statements for 2026 interim periods are available, so holding-company liquidity is stale at year-end 2025. Standard EBITDA leverage and cash interest cover cannot be computed.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: There is no sponsor-led, merger, leveraged buyout or refinancing transaction in the sources, and the run context lists no deal terms, so the transaction area carries one Insufficient Information entry for any such transaction and does not infer one. What the sources do document in the period is the following. In April 2026 the company completed the acquisition of loan receivables associated with the Lowe's commercial co-branded credit card portfolio, which it accounted for as an asset purchase and reports within Home & Auto; the annual report had expected the purchase at about 0.8 billion in the first half of 2026 and the completed amount reported is 0.7 billion, and the filed completed figure controls. New debt in 2026 was senior unsecured notes issued by Synchrony Financial in February 2026 (750) and in July 2026 (1.1 billion in two fixed-to-floating series, 600 due October 2030 and 500 due July 2037), against 500 of repayments of senior unsecured notes in the nine months; the printed ladder includes all series with their dates and rates. Securitized debt proceeds were 1,495 in the nine months against 1,000 of repayments, and the Q3 report records 750 of fixed securitized borrowings repaid in October 2026 as an event inside the filing. Preferred equity funding was the June 2026 issue of depositary shares representing 500 of Series C preferred stock at a 7.250 percent reset rate, with the first dividend in August 2026. On the distribution side the April 2026 board action approved a new repurchase programme of up to 6.5 billion with no expiry and a planned quarterly dividend increase to 0.34 per share beginning in the third quarter, and about 4.6 billion of authorisation remained at 2026-09-30. Debt raised and its liquidity effect are shown in the CP-1 handoff; use of proceeds is not stated for the notes, so it is Not supplied. The latest filing is dated 2026-10-22 and no transaction after that date is in any source.

The funding structure is deposit-led, with securitized borrowings and unsecured notes as the borrowed layers; the unsecured layer grew most in 2026 through the February and July issuances. Capital is reported above the stated minimums and the Company and the Bank are stated as well capitalized, but year-end 2025 capital ratios exist on two bases because of a presentation recast, and one earlier handoff statement is corrected below. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and transaction view: Synchrony is a consumer financing company that issues private label, dual, co-brand and general purpose credit cards, installment loans and deposit products through partner programs in five sales platforms. Its economics are tied to a short list of partner programs, the sharing of program performance through retailer share arrangements, a deposit-led funding model and heavy regulation as a savings and loan holding company with a bank subsidiary. There is no sponsor-led or leveraged transaction in the sources: the transaction section therefore records one completed asset purchase (a commercial card portfolio), the 2026 senior note, preferred stock and securitized issuance, and a larger share buyback programme. For a creditor the central questions are partner concentration and renewal, whether shareholder distributions are outrunning earnings, and how much of the funding stack sits at the holding company rather than the bank. The facts below separate what the filings state from management language and from analyst reading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: There is no sponsor-led, merger, leveraged buyout or refinancing transaction in the sources, and the run context lists no deal terms, so the transaction area carries one Insufficient Information entry for any such transaction and does not infer one. What the sources do document in the period is the following. In April 2026 the company completed the acquisition of loan receivables associated with the Lowe's commercial co-branded credit card portfolio, which it accounted for as an asset purchase and reports within Home & Auto; the annual report had expected the purchase at about 0.8 billion in the first half of 2026 and the completed amount reported is 0.7 billion, and the filed completed figure controls. New debt in 2026 was senior unsecured notes issued by Synchrony Financial in February 2026 (750) and in July 2026 (1.1 billion in two fixed-to-floating series, 600 due October 2030 and 500 due July 2037), against 500 of repayments of senior unsecured notes in the nine months; the printed ladder includes all series with their dates and rates. Securitized debt proceeds were 1,495 in the nine months against 1,000 of repayments, and the Q3 report records 750 of fixed securitized borrowings repaid in October 2026 as an event inside the filing. Preferred equity funding was the June 2026 issue of depositary shares representing 500 of Series C preferred stock at a 7.250 percent reset rate, with the first dividend in August 2026. On the distribution side the April 2026 board action approved a new repurchase programme of up to 6.5 billion with no expiry and a planned quarterly dividend increase to 0.34 per share beginning in the third quarter, and about 4.6 billion of authorisation remained at 2026-09-30. Debt raised and its liquidity effect are shown in the CP-1 handoff; use of proceeds is not stated for the notes, so it is Not supplied. The latest filing is dated 2026-10-22 and no transaction after that date is in any source.

fields.value: - Revenue durability: Evidence: the five largest programs were 54 percent of interest and fees, with expiry dates from 2030 to 2035 (F1, 10-K pages:13, 14). Risk mechanic: a single non-renewal or a partner purchase of accounts would remove a large block of receivables and fee income, while long terms give visibility to the contract dates. Credit implication: monitoring posture should track renewals and partner health; revenue visibility is high until 2030 and concentrated afterwards. The counter-evidence is the extension of the Amazon agreement and the new OnePay programme in 2025.

fields.value: - Margin and cash-flow risk: Evidence: retailer share payments rose while net charge-offs fell (F14), and other expense rose with technology and operating losses. Risk mechanic: the sharing of program performance caps the benefit of better credit, so margin gains from lower losses are shared, while cost growth is not shared. Credit implication: debt service capacity is supported by earnings that remain well above interest cost, but margin resilience depends on credit staying at current levels. The earnings fall against the prior-year quarter is a named counter to a stable-margin view.

fields.name: Quote

Risk mechanic: partner financial distress or a pricing dispute would affect volume, receivables quality and share payments together. Credit implication: concentration should be a monitoring item; no recovery conclusion is drawn here.

Risk mechanic: returning capital faster than it is earned lowers the equity cushion, and new senior notes at the holding company add claims that rank behind the Bank's deposits and the trusts' secured notes in terms of asset access. Credit implication: the key uncertainty is the pace of buybacks against the capital ratio and rating-agency targets; no sponsor exists to provide external support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Synchrony Financial has a sound fundamental credit profile with moderate, identifiable risks. The strongest support is deposit-led funding (USD 82,951 million of deposits against USD 17,025 million of borrowings at 2026-09-30), liquid assets of USD 19.5 billion and a common equity Tier 1 ratio of 12.9% that the company states exceeds regulatory minimums, with a net charge-off rate of 4.79% in Q3 2026. The weakest point is concentration: five partner programs produced 54% of interest and fees, and distributions of USD 3,262 million in the nine months of 2026 exceeded net earnings of USD 2,582 million. What decides the outcome is whether partners renew and credit losses stay near current levels while buybacks continue to lower the capital ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Synchrony Financial funds its balance sheet mainly with deposits, which were USD 82,951 million at 2026-09-30 and 83% of funding sources, while borrowings were USD 17,025 million. Because debt due within one year of that date was USD 4,500 million against liquid assets of USD 19.5 billion, near-term maturities are covered several times by liquidity even before counting the USD 2,100 million of undrawn committed securitization capacity. This lowers refinancing and liquidity risk for creditors, and the main condition is continued access to deposits and the Federal Reserve discount window, whose availability was USD 13.0 billion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business depends on a short list of partners. The five largest programs produced 54% of interest and fees and 52% of loan receivables at year-end 2025, and three of them each exceeded a tenth of interest and fees; contract expiry dates run from 2030 to 2035, and some agreements let the partner buy the accounts on termination. A loss or repricing of one program would reduce revenue and the receivables book that backs the securitized notes and supports the bank, so concentration, not leverage, is the first risk a committee should monitor.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings remain strong but are lower than a year earlier. Net earnings were USD 892 million in Q3 2026 against USD 1,077 million in the prior-year quarter, and USD 2,582 million for the nine months, while the net charge-off rate fell to 4.79% in Q3 2026 from 5.43% in Q2 2026. Retailer share arrangements of USD 3,193 million in the nine months move with program performance, so part of the benefit of better credit goes to partners and part of the pressure is absorbed by them. For debt service the only available proxy is 2.12x (pre-tax earnings plus interest expense, over interest expense, for the last twelve months), but that proxy includes deposit interest, is not an EBITDA measure, and the filings give no EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation is the main trend to monitor. Distributions in the nine months of 2026 were USD 3,262 million against net earnings of USD 2,582 million, which is 1.26x, while the common equity Tier 1 ratio on the recast basis moved from 13.5% at year-end 2025 to 12.9%, and borrowings to equity rose from 0.91x to 1.03x. New unsecured notes of USD 1,850 million and Series C preferred stock were issued in the same period. For creditors this means the equity buffer is being run down by choice and the company stays above stated regulatory minimums, so the pace of buybacks against capital targets is the variable to watch.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Structure matters for who holds which claim. Deposits are bank liabilities; securitized borrowings of USD 8,915 million are secured on restricted loans of USD 21,898 million, a ratio of 2.46x; the holding company owes about USD 7,511 million of senior and subordinated notes and relies on bank dividends and regulatory permission. Unsecured notes are 47.6% of borrowings, up from 44.6% at year-end 2025. The documented covenants restrict liens on and loss of control of the bank, and no leverage or restricted-payments test is visible, so legal capacity to distribute is not fully known.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Deposit funding is the largest strength: it is diversified between direct deposits of USD 76.2 billion and brokered deposits of USD 6.8 billion, and it lowers rollover risk relative to market funding. Liquidity is large and not dependent on committed bank lines: liquid assets were USD 19.5 billion and discount window capacity USD 13.0 billion. Credit quality was supportive in Q3 2026, with the net charge-off rate lower than in Q2 2026, delinquencies of 4.34% at 30 days and 2.06% at 90 days, and an allowance of 10.01% of receivables. Contract tenure is long, with expiry dates for the largest partners from 2030, and regulatory capital is stated as above minimums with the Bank well capitalized. Nothing documented shows sponsor extraction or creditor-adverse behaviour.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Concentration in five partner programs is the largest business weakness, and the partner purchase rights and termination terms are not in the sources. Earnings were below the prior-year quarter and a reserve build raised the provision. Distributions above earnings, a lower recast capital ratio and a rising unsecured share of borrowings reduce the margin beneath creditors. The structure places holding-company creditors behind deposits and trust investors for access to the bank's assets, and no parent-only statements for 2026 interim periods are available, so holding-company liquidity is stale at year-end 2025. Standard EBITDA leverage and cash interest cover cannot be computed.

fields.value: The credit analysis is traceable enough for committee use, with restrictions. Every figure in the financial base and every quoted business fact traces to a filed statement or note in the seven pinned documents, and the derived ratios recompute from those inputs. Traceability is strongest for funding, liquidity, capital and credit-quality figures, which come straight from filed statements. The weakest point is that three conclusions rest on documents the pack does not contain: covenant headroom, ownership and partner contract terms. Two upstream differences are logged and explained, a covenant description and the recast year-end capital ratio. What decides use is whether those documents are added before covenant or distribution capacity is relied on.
